title: Restore substantial scalp hair in severe alopecia areata with systemic treatment

concept.text: Reverse extensive autoimmune hair loss through an approved systemic medicine. JAK-pathway treatment achieved clinically substantial regrowth in a subset of patients, without establishing permanent immune tolerance. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by randomized trials in patients with at least 50% scalp hair loss, demonstrating superiority to placebo in achieving SALT ≤20, equivalent to at least 80% scalp hair coverage. Test set by: FDA; the baricitinib trials evaluated the SALT ≤20 endpoint at week 36. Reported achieved: FDA approved baricitinib (Olumiant) for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. Overlaps: DER-03, IMM-04. Sources given: [FDA announcement of first systemic alopecia areata treatment](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/31bfc85) ; [FDA review describing the alopecia treatment landscape](https://www.fda.gov/media/172964/download?attachment=).

page.title: First FDA-approved systemic treatment for adults with severe alopecia areata
page.definition: FDA approves a medicine that acts throughout the body to treat adults with severe alopecia areata, an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks hair follicles. Oral baricitinib received the first such approval on June 13, 2022. Its trials measured scalp hair loss with the Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT). A score of 20 means that 80% of the scalp has hair coverage.

goal.need: A US survey estimated that about 300,000 people had lost more than half their scalp hair to alopecia areata. Wigs conceal hair loss, and steroid injections treat individual patches. In two trials, 35% and 32% of adults taking baricitinib 4 mg daily reached at least 80% scalp hair coverage by week 36, compared with 5% and 3% on placebo. Among patients who responded after a year, 80% of those switched to placebo lost more than 20 percentage points of scalp coverage over the next 100 weeks, compared with 7% of those who continued treatment.

completion.title: FDA approves the first systemic medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata.
completion.criterion: FDA grants the first approval of a medicine that acts throughout the body with a labeled indication for treating adults with severe alopecia areata. The decision may approve a new medicine or add the indication to an existing medicine. The FDA action letter and approved labeling establish the date and scope of the approval.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, June 13, 2022 approval announcement, action letter for NDA 207924/S-007 and prescribing information, section 1.3.
completion.threshold_quote: Today’s action marks the first FDA approval of a systemic treatment (i.e. treats the entire body rather than a specific location) for alopecia areata.
completion.basis: FDA expressly identified the first systemic approval. Section 1.3 of the approved label states the adult indication. Section 14.3 describes the two baricitinib trials and their week-36 scalp coverage endpoint.

milestones.title: JAK inhibition restores complete hair coverage in treated mouse skin within 12 weeks.
milestones.criterion: A Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor reverses established alopecia areata in C3H/HeJ mice: treated skin regains complete hair coverage within 12 weeks of the start of treatment and vehicle-treated controls do not, in a peer-reviewed report that states the number of animals per group. This is an animal proof of mechanism. Prevention of disease onset without reversal of established disease is partial.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of FDA approval documents and alopecia areata guidelines found no standardized animal efficacy threshold. The criterion follows the complete-regrowth result in Xing and colleagues' published experiment.

milestones.title: Patients on an oral JAK inhibitor regain at least half their missing scalp hair by week 12.
milestones.criterion: A registered study of an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor in moderate-to-severe alopecia areata documents responders at week 12 and reports their proportion among participants. The primary endpoint defines a response as a reduction of at least 50% from the participant’s baseline SALT score. An open-label study can establish this early response.
milestones.set_by: Columbia University, registered primary outcome for NCT01950780, baseline to week 12.
milestones.threshold_quote: response defined as 50% or greater hair re-growth from baseline as assessed by SALT score at week 12.

milestones.title: More adults reach 80% scalp coverage on systemic treatment than on placebo at week 36 in phase 2.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial of adults with baseline SALT ≥50, a significantly higher proportion on systemic treatment than on placebo reaches SALT ≤20 at week 36 (P < 0.05). The primary analysis uses logistic regression and counts participants with missing outcomes as nonresponders.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company and BRAVE-AA1 investigators, phase 2 protocol NCT03570749, reported by King and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving a Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score ≤20 at week 36. Logistic regression was used with nonresponder imputation for missing data.

milestones.title: More adults reach ≥80% scalp coverage on systemic therapy than on placebo at week 36 in both phase 3 trials.
milestones.criterion: Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in adults with baseline SALT ≥50 each show that a systemic medicine is superior to placebo on the primary endpoint, the proportion of patients reaching SALT ≤20 at week 36, and the results are published after peer review or reported in regulator-approved labelling. One trial is partial.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company and BRAVE-AA investigators, phase 3 protocols NCT03570749 and NCT03899259; FDA reports the regulatory response estimates in prescribing-information section 14.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary outcome was a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36.

milestones.title: FDA accepts an application for review of a systemic treatment for adults with severe alopecia areata.
milestones.criterion: FDA accepts for substantive review a marketing application, including a supplement for a new indication, that seeks to label a systemic medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: The filing of an NDA means that FDA has made a threshold determination that the NDA is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

results.finding: C3H/HeJ mice with established alopecia areata (9 per group) regained complete hair coverage on skin treated with topical ruxolitinib or tofacitinib within 12 weeks.
results.detail: Figure 4a shows three mice per group per experiment. Figure 4b reports nine per group across the three repeats.
results.quote:
we observed complete hair regrowth 
within 12 weeks following topical therapy (Fig. 4a,b).

results.finding: All 3 reported patients with moderate-to-severe alopecia areata had near-complete hair regrowth on oral ruxolitinib within 3 to 5 months.
results.detail: The paper reports the first three treated patients. The week-12 photograph shows regrowth in one patient without quantifying the change in SALT.
results.quote:
All three ruxolitinib-
treated patients exhibited near-complete hair regrowth within 3 to  
5 months of oral treatment

results.finding: With oral ruxolitinib, 8 of 12 patients with moderate-to-severe alopecia areata regained at least half their missing scalp hair by week 12.
results.detail: The paper reports eight week-12 responders among nine eventual responders. The 66.7% cohort proportion is calculated using all 12 treated participants as the denominator.
results.quote: resulting in the majority (8 of 9) of responders achieving at least 50% regrowth by the week 12 visit.

results.finding: In BRAVE-AA1 (N=110), the oral baricitinib 1-mg arm (n=28) had a lower SALT 30 response rate at the first interim analysis.
results.detail: The excerpt gives neither the numerical SALT 30 rate nor a week-12 SALT 50 result.
results.quote: The baricitinib 1-mg dose was dropped after the first interim analysis based on lower SALT 30  response rate.

results.finding: In BRAVE-AA1 (N=110), 51.9% of adults on oral baricitinib 4 mg (n=27) reached SALT ≤20 at week 36, significantly more than on placebo.
results.detail: Both the 2-mg and 4-mg comparisons met P < 0.05. The excerpt leaves the masking design unverified.
results.quote: At week 36, the proportion of patients achieving a SALT score of ≤20 was significantly greater in baricitinib 2-mg (33.3%, P = .016) and 4-mg (51.9%, P = .001) groups versus placebo (3.6%).

results.finding: Oral baricitinib 4 mg improved week-36 SALT ≤20 response by 32.6 percentage points versus placebo in each phase 3 trial (n=654 and n=546).
results.detail: The excerpt establishes superiority in both trials. Double blinding is the sole criterion element left unverified by the supplied text.
results.quote: In two phase 3 trials involving patients with severe alopecia areata, oral baricitinib was superior to placebo with respect to hair regrowth at 36 weeks.

results.finding: In JAHO phase 2 (N=110), 25.9% of adults assigned to oral baricitinib 4 mg reached SALT50 at week 12.
results.detail: The phase 2 dose-selection analysis used SALT30 at week 12 and SALT50 at week 16.

results.finding: In JAHO phase 2 (N=110), oral baricitinib 4 mg increased week-36 SALT ≤20 response by 48.3 percentage points versus placebo.

results.finding: Across both trials (N=1,200), oral baricitinib 4 mg increased week-36 attainment of at least 80% scalp coverage by about 30 percentage points versus placebo in each trial.
results.detail: The absolute differences from the reported rounded rates were 30 percentage points in AA-1 and 29 in AA-2.
results.quote: In Trial AA-1, 22% of the 184 patients who received 2 milligrams of Olumiant and 35% of the 281 patients who received 4 milligrams of Olumiant achieved adequate scalp hair coverage, compared to 5% of the 189 patients who received a placebo.

results.finding: FDA approved oral baricitinib, the first systemic treatment for adults with severe alopecia areata, on June 13, 2022 (supporting trials N=1,200).

results.finding: Topical ruxolitinib or tofacitinib restored complete back-skin hair coverage within 12 weeks in C3H/HeJ mice with established alopecia areata (3 mice per group).
results.detail: The vehicle-control outcome comes from Figure 4. Untreated abdominal skin on drug-treated mice also remained alopecic.
results.quote: we observed complete hair regrowth within 12 weeks following topical therapy

results.finding: In the oral ruxolitinib pilot for moderate-to-severe alopecia areata (3 patients reported), Figure 4f shows scalp hair regrowth at week 12.
results.detail: The 12-week observation is photographic. The near-complete regrowth reported for all three patients spans 3 to 5 months.
results.quote: Treatment of patient 3 with AA, who had hair loss involving >80% of his scalp at baseline, with ruxolitinib and hair regrowth after 12 weeks of oral treatment.

results.finding: With oral ruxolitinib (n=12), 8 of 9 eventual responders regained at least half their missing scalp hair by week 12.
results.detail: The primary endpoint applied the ≥50% reduction from baseline SALT at the end of treatment, which varied from 3 to 6 months. The reported week-12 result used the same threshold.
results.quote: the majority (8 of 9) of responders achieving at least 50% regrowth by the week 12 visit.

results.finding: Across AA-1 and AA-2 (N=1,200), baricitinib 4 mg increased week-36 SALT ≤20 response by 30 percentage points over placebo in each trial.
results.detail: The 95% CI for the 4 mg difference was 23 to 36 percentage points in each trial. The label establishes the adult indication added in June 2022. The action letter, exact approval date, and first-in-class status are absent from the supplied text.

results.finding: Oral baricitinib improved scalp coverage by week 12 in BRAVE-AA2. The two phase 3 trials enrolled 1,200 adults combined.
results.detail: The SmPC gives neither the BRAVE-AA2 sample size separately nor the numerical week-12 responder proportion.
results.quote: In both studies, a significantly greater proportion of patients randomised to baricitinib 4 mg once daily achieved a SALT ≤ 20 at week 36 compared to placebo, starting as early as week 8 in study BRAVE-AA1 and week 12 in study BRAVE-AA2.

results.finding: Across 1,200 adults in two phase 3 trials, 34.0% of those on baricitinib 4 mg reached SALT ≤20 at week 36.
results.detail: The numerical rates are pooled. The SmPC explicitly reports significant superiority over placebo in each trial.
results.quote: In both studies, a significantly greater proportion of patients randomised to baricitinib 4 mg once daily achieved a SALT ≤ 20 at week 36 compared to placebo, starting as early as week 8 in study BRAVE-AA1 and week 12 in study BRAVE-AA2.

results.finding: In JAHO phase 2 (110 adults), oral baricitinib significantly improved week-36 AA-IGA response with a ≥2-point gain versus placebo.
results.detail: The excerpt identifies the phase 2 efficacy table but omits its data. The phase 3 analyses explicitly report SALT ≤20 at week 36 and describe logistic regression with nonresponder imputation.
